title: Word slips: Positive-ink invoice
summary: String scanning. Add the positive numbers.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`line` is text. A character is one letter, digit, space, or punctuation mark.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `wordLengths`. Read `line` from left to right. Here, a word is a group of characters with no spaces inside it. Record the length of each word. Ignore extra spaces before, after, or between words. For "a  cat", `wordLengths` is [1, 3].
2. Add only the numbers in `wordLengths` that are greater than 0. Store the sum in `positiveTotal`.
3. Complete `wordSlipsPositiveInkInvoice` so it returns `positiveTotal`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `line` is "ok  zoo", then `wordLengths` is [2, 3] and `wordSlipsPositiveInkInvoice` returns 5.

Rules
- If `wordLengths` is empty, return 0.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `line` is "inkk paaaper".
TEST DATA 2: `line` is "QQ qQQ".

The last problem also counts positions from 1.
constraints: Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
The text uses ASCII characters (a basic character set). Only an ordinary space separates words.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
hints: Work through TEST DATA 1 by hand. Write down `wordLengths` before you look for the answer.
